title: Simultaneous extraction of proteins and metabolites from cells in culture
author: Sapcariu, Kanashova, et al.
materials: The following procedure is for adherent cells cultured on a 6-well multiplate. For cells cultured on a 12-well multiplate, divide the amount of extraction fluids by two. Amounts for other cell culture vessels should be adjusted accordingly.1.Retain medium for quantification of cellular consumption and secretion of metabolites.2.Wash cells with 1 mL 0.9% NaCl. Phosphate buffer solution is avoided because it would create a large phosphate peak during mass spectrometric analysis, masking lower intensity metabolites.3.Quench cells by adding 400 μL methanol at −20 °C followed by 400 μL Millipore H2O on ice. As soon as the methanol has been added, place the multiwell plate on ice for the next steps.4.Scrape wells with a cell scraper. Make sure that as few cells as possible remain attached to the plate through careful and thorough scraping.5.Transfer cell extract into an Eppendorf tube containing 400 μL chloroform at −20 °C.6.Agitate cells in a tube shaker (pre-cooled to 4 °C) for 20 min at 1400 rpm, followed by 5 min of centrifugation at a minimum of 16,100 × g at 4 °C.

The following procedure is for suspension cells cultured on a 6-well multiplate. For cells cultured on a 12-well multiplate, divide the amount of extraction fluids by two. Amounts for other cell culture vessels should be adjusted accordingly.1.Centrifuge cells in medium at 250 × g for 5 min to pellet the cells, collect medium and retain for quantification of cellular consumption and secretion of metabolites.2.Wash cells with 1 mL 0.9% NaCl, centrifuge at 250 × g for 5 min to pellet the cells, then discard NaCl.3.Quench cells by adding 400 μL methanol at −20 °C and 400 μL Millipore H2O on ice.4.Add 400 μL chloroform at −20 °C to the cells, transfer to Eppendorf tubes.5.Agitate cells in a tube shaker (pre-cooled to 4 °C) for 20 min at 1400 rpm, followed by 5 min of centrifugation at a minimum of 16,100 × g at 4 °C.

For cell types which are both suspended and adherent in culture, the procedure must be modified somewhat to avoid over-dilution of the metabolites. The following procedure is for cells cultured on a 6-well multiplate. Amounts for other cell culture vessels should be adjusted accordingly.1.Collect the medium from the plate, centrifuge cells in medium at 250 × g for 5 min to pellet the cells, collect medium and retain for quantification of cellular consumption and secretion of metabolites.2.Wash the adherent fraction and suspension fraction of cells each with 1 mL 0.9% NaCl, centrifuge at 250 × g for 5 min to pellet the cells, then discard NaCl.3.Quench cells by adding 200 μL methanol at −20 °C and 200 μL Millipore H2O on ice to both the suspension cell pellet and the adherent cell pellet. As soon as the methanol has been added, place the multiwell plate on ice for the next steps.4.Scrape wells containing adherent cell fraction with a cell scraper. Make sure that, as few cells as possible remain attached to the plate through careful and thorough scraping. Transfer the quenched cells to the corresponding non-adherent cell fraction.5.Add 400 μL chloroform at −20 °C to the cells, transfer to Eppendorf tubes.6.Agitate cells in a tube shaker (pre-cooled to 4 °C) for 20 min at 1400 rpm, followed by 5 min of centrifugation at a minimum of 16,100 × g at 4 °C.

steps.title: Extract from adherent cells
steps.instruction: Simultaneous extraction of metabolites and proteins from adherent cells grown in a 6‑well plate (divide all volumes by two for a 12‑well plate).

substeps.instruction: 1. Retain the culture medium in a separate tube for later quantification of cellular consumption and secretion of metabolites.
2. Wash each well with 1 mL of 0.9 % NaCl (avoid phosphate buffer to prevent phosphate peaks in MS).
3. Quench metabolism by adding 400 µL of methanol pre‑cooled to –20 °C, immediately followed by 400 µL of Millipore H₂O kept on ice; place the plate on ice as soon as the methanol is added.
4. Scrape the cells thoroughly with a cell scraper, ensuring minimal cells remain attached to the plate.
5. Transfer the entire well extract into an Eppendorf tube that already contains 400 µL of chloroform pre‑cooled to –20 °C.
6. Agitate the tube in a pre‑cooled (4 °C) tube shaker for 20 min at 1400 rpm, then centrifuge for 5 min at ≥16 100 × g, 4 °C.

steps.title: Extract from suspension cells
steps.instruction: Simultaneous extraction of metabolites and proteins from suspension cells cultured in a 6‑well plate (divide all volumes by two for a 12‑well plate).

substeps.instruction: 1. Centrifuge the cell suspension (still in medium) at 250 × g for 5 min; collect and keep the supernatant medium for later metabolite quantification.
2. Wash the cell pellet with 1 mL of 0.9 % NaCl, centrifuge again at 250 × g for 5 min, and discard the NaCl wash.
3. Quench by adding 400 µL of methanol (–20 °C) and 400 µL of Millipore H₂O on ice.
4. Add 400 µL of chloroform (–20 °C) to the quenched cells, then transfer the mixture to an Eppendorf tube.
5. Agitate in a 4 °C tube shaker for 20 min at 1400 rpm, followed by 5 min centrifugation at ≥16 100 × g, 4 °C.

steps.title: Extract from mixed adherent/suspension cultures
steps.instruction: Simultaneous extraction for cell types that have both adherent and suspension fractions in a 6‑well plate (adjust volumes for other plate formats).

substeps.instruction: 1. Collect the medium from the plate, centrifuge at 250 × g for 5 min, keep the supernatant for metabolite analysis, and pellet the cells.
2. Wash both the adherent fraction (still attached to the plate) and the suspension pellet with 1 mL of 0.9 % NaCl each, centrifuge at 250 × g for 5 min, and discard the NaCl wash.
3. Quench both fractions by adding 200 µL of methanol (–20 °C) and 200 µL of Millipore H₂O on ice; place the plate on ice immediately after methanol addition.
4. Scrape the adherent cells with a cell scraper, transfer the scraped material into the tube containing the suspension pellet, ensuring as few cells as possible remain on the plate.
5. Add 400 µL of chloroform (–20 °C) to the combined cell suspension, then transfer the mixture to an Eppendorf tube.
6. Agitate in a 4 °C tube shaker for 20 min at 1400 rpm, then centrifuge for 5 min at ≥16 100 × g, 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect and dry polar phase (adherent cells)
steps.instruction: Separate and dry the polar (upper) phase after the biphasic extraction for adherent‑cell samples (divide polar‑phase volumes by two for a 12‑well plate).

substeps.instruction: 1. Carefully pipette 300 µL of the upper polar phase into a glass vial without disturbing the interphase.
2. Evaporate the polar phase in a rotary vacuum evaporator set to –4 °C until completely dry (or overnight).
3. After drying, raise the evaporator temperature to room temperature and hold for 30 min before removing the vial to avoid condensation; cap the vial and store at –80 °C until analysis.

4. Remove any remaining polar phase while avoiding the interphase: tilt the Eppendorf tube to ~45°, let the interphase shift away, and optionally transfer 300 µL of the lower non‑polar phase to a glass vial for drying (same conditions) if non‑polar analysis is required; otherwise discard the non‑polar phase carefully.
5. Wash the interphase with 300 µL of methanol (–20 °C) and centrifuge for 10 min at ≥16 100 × g, 4 °C.

6. Remove the methanol; the washed interphase can be processed immediately for protein or mRNA extraction, or add 50 µL of methanol (–20 °C) and store at –80 °C for later nucleic‑acid/protein extraction.

steps.title: Optional amino‑acid hydrolysis of interphase
steps.instruction: Hydrolyze the interphase to release amino acids for metabolomics (optional step).

substeps.instruction: 1. After methanol removal, add 400 µL of 6 M HCl to the interphase in a tightly sealed tube.
2. Heat the tube overnight at 100 °C.
3. Transfer 100 µL of the hydrolysate to a glass vial and dry in a rotary vacuum evaporator at –4 °C until dry.
4. Store the dried sample at –80 °C until LC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Process interphase for protein analysis
steps.instruction: Prepare the protein‑containing interphase for quantification and digestion.

substeps.instruction: 1. Dry the washed interphase (containing proteins) in a rotary vacuum evaporator at 35 °C for 15 min.
2. Resuspend the dried protein pellet in 60 µL of denaturation buffer; sonicate for 1 min to disrupt aggregates.
3. Determine protein concentration with a Bradford assay and adjust to obtain exactly 100 µg of protein.
4. In a new Eppendorf tube, add 2 µL of 10 mM TCEP solution to the 100 µg protein sample and incubate 30 min at room temperature to reduce disulfide bonds.
5. Add 1 µL of 100 mM chloroacetamide solution to 10 µL of the reduced protein sample (final volume 11 µL) and incubate 20 min at room temperature for cysteine alkylation.

6. Add 4 µL of Lys‑C protease to the alkylated sample and incubate 3 h at room temperature for digestion. After digestion, optionally acidify to pH < 2.5 by adding 10 µL of 10 % TFA to stop the reaction; then proceed to fractionation, stage‑tip desalting, and LC‑MS/MS analysis.

steps.title: Alternative trypsin digestion (optional)
steps.instruction: Digest the protein sample with trypsin instead of Lys‑C (optional pathway).

substeps.instruction: 1. Dilute the protein solution with 4× ABC buffer, ensuring the final urea concentration does not exceed 2 M.
2. Add 2 µL of trypsin to the diluted sample and incubate overnight at room temperature.
3. Stop the digestion by adding 10 µL of 10 % TFA, lowering the pH to <2.5.
4. Proceed to fractionation, stage‑tip desalting, and LC‑MS/MS analysis.

steps.title: Extract metabolites from culture medium (high glucose)
steps.instruction: Prepare extraction samples from high‑glucose (25 mM) culture medium; scale volumes proportionally for lower‑glucose media.

substeps.instruction: 1. Pre‑chill Eppendorf tubes and add 450 µL of 8:1 methanol:H₂O (pre‑cooled to –20 °C) to each tube.
2. Mix the culture medium well, then transfer 50 µL of medium into the chilled extraction fluid; vortex briefly to mix.
3. Centrifuge the tubes for 5 min at ≥16 100 × g, 4 °C.
4. Transfer 100 µL of the clear supernatant to a glass vial and dry in a rotary vacuum evaporator at –4 °C; cap the vial and store at –80 °C until analysis.
